why: Same notions on both sides: B writes out ScRetraction.tangent (tangentMap R.U R '' E.tangentSet R.U), so the main conjunct proposition_2_4 is B verbatim (A_to_B and the first conjunct of B_to_A are rfl-level). The other conjuncts of A are proof-internal helpers: r' ∘ r = r on U when r(U) ⊆ r'(U'), the fixed-point description TO = {p ∈ TU | Tr(p) = p}, and the inclusion version r(U) ⊆ r'(U') ⇒ Tr(TU) ⊆ Tr'(TU'). They are not consequences of B (which only compares retractions with equal images); B_to_A proves them directly by the text's argument (chain rule theorem_1_21 for r' ∘ r = r, tangentMap_tangentMap), avoiding the banned lemmas. So B_to_A uses B only for the proposition_2_4 conjunct; the helper conjuncts are proved outright.
overlap: B_to_A shares 100 project theorems (counting auxiliary _proof_ terms) with the formal proof, all chain-rule / sc-calculus infrastructure (theorem_1_21, theorem_1_21', IsSc1.tangentMap_congr, ScRetraction.tangentMap_tangentMap, tangentMap_mapsTo, apply_eq_self_of_mem_retract, mem_retract_iff, lvlSet lemmas); these come from re-proving the helper conjuncts (inclusion version and fixed-point description), not from the proposition_2_4 conjunct, which is B itself.
